systems.title: Start with the question, then follow the evidence
systems.description: Identification, safe setup and the habits that make diagnosis useful.
systems.introduction: A good repair starts before the first bolt comes out. Identify the car’s engine and equipment, describe exactly what happens, and choose the procedure that answers that question. Treat diagnosis as detective work: each check should narrow the possibilities, not create a new shopping list.

howItWorks.title: Make the symptom repeatable
howItWorks.body: Note when the concern happens: starting, idling, accelerating, braking or turning. Ford’s diagnostic methods normally assume the concern is present during the test, unless that test says otherwise. An intermittent problem needs its conditions understood before a replacement decision is justified.

howItWorks.title: Check the basics first
howItWorks.body: Previous repairs, a weak electrical supply, damaged wiring, loose connections and leaks can affect several systems. Preliminary checks give later measurements a trustworthy starting point. Record trouble codes before following the appropriate circuit or system test.

howItWorks.title: Use the tool the test requires
howItWorks.body: Reading a code, watching live data and commanding a module output are different capabilities. A scan tool, multimeter and correctly sized terminal probes each answer different questions. Use the specified setup so the measurement does not damage the thing you are checking.

systems.title: Follow the engine’s flow of air, fuel, movement and oil
systems.description: The moving parts, lubrication and timing that turn combustion into useful rotation.
systems.introduction: An engine is easier to understand as a few connected jobs. Air and fuel enter, combustion pushes the pistons, and the crankshaft turns that movement into rotation. Valve timing keeps the breathing in step; oil and coolant let the machinery survive the heat and load.

howItWorks.title: Keep the engine identity in view
howItWorks.body: This library includes several engines with different layouts. The 3.7L V6, 2.3L EcoBoost and V8 procedures are not interchangeable. Engine labels and identification information help match parts, diagrams and specifications to the actual vehicle.

howItWorks.title: Breathing has a schedule
howItWorks.body: Camshafts open the intake and exhaust valves in time with the crankshaft. Variable camshaft timing can change those events as conditions change. The timing chains inside the engine do a different job from the accessory belts outside it.

howItWorks.title: Oil has more than one job
howItWorks.body: Pressurized oil supplies loaded bearings and, on the described engines, oil-controlled timing components. Cleanliness matters during engine work: contamination can damage small passages and precision surfaces. An oil-level check, a pressure test and a bearing-clearance measurement answer different questions.

systems.title: Move heat out without keeping the engine too cold
systems.description: Coolant circulation, temperature control and the difference between a symptom and its cause.
systems.introduction: The cooling system is a heat-transport loop. Coolant collects heat inside the engine, carries it to the radiator and releases it to the outside air. The thermostat controls the radiator path so the engine can warm up as well as stay cool.

howItWorks.title: Trace the loop
howItWorks.body: In the 3.7L description, the accessory-belt-driven pump sends coolant through the block and cylinder heads. A separate branch supplies the heater core. When the thermostat allows radiator flow, heat moves from the coolant into the passing air.

howItWorks.title: Know what the bottle does
howItWorks.body: The degas bottle provides expansion space, removes air, supplies reserve coolant and serves as the service fill point on that system. Coolant level, circulation and airflow are separate checks; seeing coolant in the bottle does not establish that all three are working.

howItWorks.title: Warm-up behavior depends on the design
howItWorks.body: The 3.7L uses a cold-side thermostat at the lower radiator hose connection. During warm-up it can open and close repeatedly as cooler returning coolant reaches it. Use the exact engine’s operating description and tests instead of assuming every thermostat behaves the same way.

howItWorks.title: Treat overheat messages as information to act on
howItWorks.body: Fail-safe cooling is a protective response to excessive temperature, not a repair. The engine-specific description explains the warning stages and operating limits. Stop and address the cause according to that procedure rather than using the protection strategy as a way to keep driving.

systems.title: Separate the liquid-fuel path from the vapor path
systems.description: Fuel delivery, metering, air control and evaporative emissions.
systems.introduction: The fuel system must deliver the right amount of fuel while keeping it contained. It helps to picture two paths: liquid fuel travels toward the engine, while fuel vapor is managed by the evaporative-emissions system. A problem in one path does not automatically identify a failed part in the other.

howItWorks.title: Tank, pump, rail, injectors
howItWorks.body: The tank pump supplies the delivery system, the rail distributes fuel and the injectors meter it. The 3.7L description includes a tank module with a filter and pressure-control features. Its fuel-level sender measures quantity; it does not measure the pump’s delivery performance.

howItWorks.title: Air and fuel must agree
howItWorks.body: The throttle and engine controller manage incoming air and fuel delivery together. Port-injected and direct-injected engines use different arrangements, so pressures, components and release procedures must come from the correct engine section.

howItWorks.title: Containment remains part of the job
howItWorks.body: Fuel and vapor tubes, couplings and the filler assembly all belong to the system. The described capless filler is not intended to be modified. Before opening fuel plumbing, use the matching safety and pressure-release instructions; switching off the engine alone does not establish that pressure is gone.

systems.title: Match engine speed and torque to the job
systems.description: Manual and automatic gearboxes, clutch operation and transmission-specific service.
systems.introduction: The transmission changes the relationship between engine rotation and road speed. Lower gears provide more turning force at the wheels; higher gears let the car travel faster for a given engine speed. The way a manual car connects the engine to its gearbox differs from the way an automatic does it.

howItWorks.title: A manual clutch controls the connection
howItWorks.body: The friction disc connects engine rotation to the transmission when clamped. Releasing it allows their speeds to differ while you stop or change gear. The pedal hydraulics and release mechanism operate that connection; they are separate from the gears inside the transmission.

howItWorks.title: Synchronizers help a manual shift
howItWorks.body: Synchronizers bring rotating parts to compatible speeds before engagement. The MT82 description identifies a fully synchronized six-speed gearbox and different synchronizer arrangements by gear. A difficult shift can involve release, linkage or internal operation, so follow the symptom’s diagnostic path.

howItWorks.title: Identify the unit before choosing instructions
howItWorks.body: The library includes MT82, 3160 and 6R80 material. A fluid, fastener or procedure for one is not automatically appropriate for another. Use the transmission identification information and the exact section before comparing specifications.

systems.title: Follow rotation from the gearbox to both rear wheels
systems.description: Driveshafts, the differential, halfshafts and their joints.
systems.introduction: Once the transmission has selected the ratio, the driveline carries its output to the rear wheels. The driveshaft turns the differential; the differential drives a halfshaft on each side. Each connection has to transmit torque while allowing the vehicle’s mounts and suspension to move.

howItWorks.title: The differential makes corners possible
howItWorks.body: The drive pinion turns the ring gear and differential case. Inside, the gear arrangement allows the two halfshafts to rotate at different speeds when a corner requires it. Limited-slip designs influence how torque is shared, and the manual distinguishes the fitted differential types.

howItWorks.title: Precision setup matters
howItWorks.body: Backlash describes clearance between meshing gears; bearing preload describes how the bearings are loaded. They are different adjustments. New gears or bearings need the specified setup rather than a “tight enough” judgment.

howItWorks.title: Separate noise, vibration and leakage
howItWorks.body: A rotating vibration, a load-dependent whine and a leaking seal point toward different checks. The driveshaft, joints, differential and wheel ends are connected, so where you hear a noise is only the start of the investigation.

systems.title: Let the wheels move while keeping them controlled
systems.description: Springs, dampers, arms, wheel bearings and alignment.
systems.introduction: Suspension does more than soften bumps. It supports the vehicle, guides each wheel’s movement and helps keep the tire usefully connected to the road. Springs carry load; dampers control motion; arms and links decide the path the wheel can take.

howItWorks.title: Spring and damper are a team
howItWorks.body: A spring compresses and stores energy when a wheel meets a bump. The shock absorber resists the resulting movement so the car does not keep bouncing. On the described rear suspension the shock mounts to the lower arm and works alongside the spring.

howItWorks.title: Independent does not mean disconnected
howItWorks.body: The rear wheels can react to road imperfections independently, guided by upper and lower arms. The stabilizer bar links the sides to help resist body roll. Toe links and other locating parts maintain the wheel’s intended orientation through movement.

howItWorks.title: Alignment describes angles
howItWorks.body: Toe is the wheel’s direction from above; camber is its tilt from the front or rear. These are measured relationships, not just appearances. Repairing a mounting part and checking the resulting alignment are related steps when the procedure requires them.

systems.title: Your input sets the direction; electric assistance supplies the help
systems.description: How EPAS senses steering effort and turns it into controlled assistance.
systems.introduction: The steering wheel gives the car its direction, but you do not have to supply all the turning effort yourself. Electronic power assist steering—EPAS—uses an electric motor to help move the steering rack. Its controller continually adjusts that help to the driver’s input and the vehicle’s operating conditions.

howItWorks.title: It measures effort as well as motion
howItWorks.body: A torque sensor measures the driver’s twisting effort through the relative movement across a torsion bar. The power steering control module, or PSCM, uses that signal as its main assistance input. Steering angle and steering torque are different measurements: where the wheel points is not the same as how hard you are turning it.

howItWorks.title: The motor helps move the rack
howItWorks.body: A reversible motor drives the rack through a toothed belt and pulley-bearing arrangement. Tie rods carry the rack’s movement to the front wheels. The motor, controller and torque sensor are serviced as the steering-gear assembly in this description; the tie rods and bellows boots are separately serviceable.

howItWorks.title: Assistance changes with conditions
howItWorks.body: At lower speeds the system provides more help for maneuvering; at higher speeds it reduces assistance for road feel. The controller also uses network information and compensates for effects such as road camber—the road’s side-to-side slope—within the system’s designed limits.

howItWorks.title: A heavier wheel needs context
howItWorks.body: The system can reduce assistance for conditions such as voltage or temperature concerns, or remove electrical assistance for a critical fault. Mechanical steering remains in that described failure mode, but the effort becomes heavy. A warning or sudden change in effort calls for the relevant diagnostic path, not an assumption that the entire gear has failed.

systems.title: Turn motion into heat, with control at each wheel
systems.description: Friction brakes, hydraulic assistance, ABS and stability control.
systems.introduction: Pressing the brake pedal creates hydraulic pressure that makes the calipers press pads against the rotating discs. Friction slows the wheels and produces heat. Electronic control adds another layer: it can adjust pressure at individual wheels to help preserve steering and stability.

howItWorks.title: Separate the mechanical and hydraulic jobs
howItWorks.body: Pads and discs provide the friction surfaces. Caliper pistons apply them using brake-fluid pressure. The master cylinder creates pressure from pedal input, while the booster helps reduce driver effort. Each part contributes, so a pedal or stopping concern needs the matching test rather than a guess.

howItWorks.title: ABS and stability control share hardware
howItWorks.body: ABS helps prevent wheel lock during braking. Stability control can adjust braking and engine torque to help control a skid; traction control addresses wheel spin during acceleration. The hydraulic control unit and sensor information support these different functions.

howItWorks.title: Match the brake package
howItWorks.body: This library includes different caliper and pad arrangements. Choose the installed piston count or performance package before using a pad procedure. Noise and pedal pulsation can be normal during active ABS intervention, but that does not explain every brake noise or every change in pedal feel.

systems.title: Track both electrical power and the information riding beside it
systems.description: Charging, batteries, circuits, connectors and module communication.
systems.introduction: Electrical diagnosis becomes less mysterious when you separate two questions: does the device have the power and ground it needs, and is it receiving the right command? Modern modules share information, so one sensor reading can support several different vehicle systems.

howItWorks.title: The battery and generator work together
howItWorks.body: The battery stores energy; the belt-driven generator supplies electrical power when the engine runs. The generator converts its internal AC output to DC, and its regulator follows the control strategy. The charging system also monitors battery and generator information to manage loads.

howItWorks.title: A connection must work under load
howItWorks.body: A wire can appear connected or pass a simple continuity check while excessive resistance prevents it carrying enough current. Voltage-drop testing examines a working circuit. Correct probes preserve terminal fit so the test itself does not introduce a new fault.

howItWorks.title: Messages have their own paths
howItWorks.body: Vehicle modules exchange information across communication networks, sometimes through a gateway. A missing message is different from a missing power supply. Network tests and module fault codes help identify which path needs attention before a controller is condemned.

systems.title: Control temperature, humidity and where the air goes
systems.description: Heating, air conditioning, blower airflow and air-door control.
systems.introduction: Cabin comfort comes from several separate jobs. The blower moves air, the heater core can warm it, the evaporator can cool and dry it, and internal doors choose its path. Thinking in those stages helps separate weak airflow from air at the wrong temperature.

howItWorks.title: Heating uses engine heat
howItWorks.body: Hot coolant flows through the heater core while cabin air passes across it. A heating concern can therefore involve the cooling circuit as well as the cabin air-control parts.

howItWorks.title: Air conditioning also removes moisture
howItWorks.body: During A/C operation, the evaporator cools the passing air and reduces its humidity. The compressor and condenser belong to the refrigerant loop that moves this heat outside. Refrigerant work uses dedicated recovery and charging procedures.

howItWorks.title: Know which controls are fitted
howItWorks.body: The dual automatic temperature-control system can maintain separate driver and passenger settings and adjust its operation automatically. Electronic manual temperature control has its own description and tests. The buttons may look familiar, but the control strategies and components must match the fitted system.

systems.title: Structure, sealing and the everyday moving parts
systems.description: Body panels, mounts, weatherstrips, glass, trim and noise control.
systems.introduction: The body is both the structure that locates major assemblies and the enclosure that keeps the cabin usable. Alignment, seals and insulation work together. A wind noise, a water leak and a door that closes poorly can share a fitting problem without having the same repair.

howItWorks.title: Mounting points set relationships
howItWorks.body: The subframes provide attachment points for suspension and other major parts. Body or underbody misalignment can affect wheel alignment, drivetrain operation and opening fit. Structural dimensions matter beyond the appearance of a panel gap.

howItWorks.title: Choose the material for its job
howItWorks.body: Weatherstrip seals a moving opening, seam sealer closes panel joints and insulation reduces transmitted noise. Adhesives, sealants and lubricants are not interchangeable merely because they all come in a tube or can.

howItWorks.title: Find the path before treating the symptom
howItWorks.body: Water and noise can travel before they become noticeable inside. Follow the appropriate body diagnostic method to locate the entry or contact point. Correct fit and attachment are as important as the visible condition of a seal.

systems.title: A coordinated safety system with dedicated service rules
systems.description: Seat belts, airbags, pretensioners, sensors and restraint-system control.
systems.introduction: Seat belts and the supplemental restraint system work together to manage occupant movement in a collision. The restraints control module watches sensor and occupant information and decides whether particular deployable components are needed. Service procedures preserve that carefully controlled behavior.

howItWorks.title: The controller makes a coordinated decision
howItWorks.body: The restraints control module receives information from occupant-classification equipment and other sensors. When the event meets its criteria, it supplies the current needed to deploy the appropriate components. Not every impact produces the same response.

howItWorks.title: Connector details are functional
howItWorks.body: Deployable-component connectors use connector-position-assurance tabs and shorting-bar arrangements. A plug can appear attached while an incompletely seated assurance tab still causes a diagnostic fault. Correct locking is part of the circuit’s intended operation.

howItWorks.title: Use the restraint-specific procedure
howItWorks.body: Airbags and pretensioners are deployable devices, not ordinary electrical loads. Follow the exact depowering, handling, testing and restoration steps for the selected repair. General-purpose jumper or resistance tests must not replace the prescribed restraint-system method.
